The 3 second pass deadline (vs the 30 second route timeout at backend/src/index.ts:49) means GET never waits (fire-and-forget with .catch) and POST waits at most 3 seconds before proceeding unreconciled - in that case the unique {slot,date} index still forces the later duplicate insert to 409, so a timeout cannot open a double-book path.

Outbound Razorpay fetches on a public GET: max 10 rows per attempt, all launched concurrently, max 1 attempt per 60 seconds from the previous pass per process, rotated by reconciledAt so abandoned rows cannot starve newer ones; abandoned rows are never deleted, only rotated to the back of the queue; no createdAt window exists, so a payment captured any time after order creation is still reconciled.

Payment truth comes only from server-side orders.fetch; client claims are never trusted; the webhook path still cannot mark slots paid (payments.ts is protected) - defence-in-depth stays out of this slice.

Reconcile runs on read, so a just-paid slot can show free until the next availability or order call; closing that window fully needs the frontend confirm call (outside owned paths) or a webhook edit (protected), both Jay's to allow.
